sections.title: 56. Repository 058 bottom line
sections.content:
Repository 058 `Video-Tools` is best understood as **OpenCV Video-to-Frame Extraction Utility**. Its strongest direct contribution is **OpenCV `VideoCapture`, video metadata inspection, frame iteration/decoding**. Its maturity is **2.3/5 — functional local utility** and its principal limitations are **Comment says “30 frames per second,” but implementation saves every source frame rather than resampling to 30 FPS; Potential divide-by-zero/invalid duration if source FPS is zero; `cv2.imwrite` return value is not checked**.

The correct portfolio use is precise: preserve the chronology, credit executed/authored work, attach provenance, and state missing layers explicitly. The repository should neither be dismissed because it is a learning artifact nor inflated into a production system because its title names an advanced field.

**End of Repository 058 analysis.**

The implementation uses the standard `read()` loop until decoding fails/end-of-stream, then writes frames with zero-padded sequential names. This is simple and understandable, making the dataflow easy to audit: video stream → decoded frame → filesystem JPEG.

## 8. 30-FPS comment mismatch

The leading comment says the function extracts “30 frames per second,” but there is no temporal resampling logic. Every source frame is saved. If the input is 24, 30, 60 or variable FPS, the output count follows decoded frames, not a fixed 30-Hz sampling policy. This is a documentation/behavior mismatch worth preserving as an engineering lesson.
